transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, uh… I came in because I just can’t seem to sit still. It’s like there’s a motor running inside me all day, like I’m wound up and I can’t shut it off. If I’m at church and I’m supposed to be sitting there quiet, or here at the clinic waiting, or even just at home, I start feeling trapped in my own body. Like I have to get up, move around, do something with my hands, walk somewhere—anything.

It’s not just being a little restless, you know? It feels uncomfortable, like pressure building up if I try to stay still too long. I’ll be sitting there thinking, “Just stay put,” but my body doesn’t want to listen. That’s really why I’m here, because it’s been wearing me down.
Have you started or changed the dose of any new medications recently, especially anything like an antipsychotic, anti-nausea drug, or antidepressant?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, not that I can remember. I haven’t had anything new like that started recently, at least not something I’d recognize by those names.

I’m not always good with medication names, to be honest—like if you asked me the exact name of something, I might have to go look at the bottle or ask the pharmacy. But as far as I know, nobody recently put me on a new medicine or changed a dose and then this started happening. I don’t think it’s connected to something like that.
Do you notice that this restless, need-to-move feeling is worse in the evening or at night, especially in your legs, and that moving your legs specifically gives you relief?

I’m not really sure it’s like that, no. I mean… I haven’t noticed it being specifically worse at night or just in the evening, and I wouldn’t say it’s only my legs or that moving my legs fixes it.

It’s more like I just feel restless in general, like my whole body wants to be doing something. But as far as that thing where it’s mainly the legs at night and moving them gives relief… I don’t think I’ve paid attention to that, or at least it hasn’t stood out to me that way.

Along with this urge to move, do you also find yourself worrying a lot or having anxious thoughts running through your mind, or is it mainly just the physical feeling of needing to move without much worry attached to it?

It’s more the physical thing, I think. I mean, I do get frustrated about it because it wears me out, but it doesn’t feel like I’m sitting there thinking a bunch of worried thoughts, like, “Oh no, what’s going to happen?” It’s more like my body is just… running. Like there’s a motor inside me that won’t shut off.

If I’m at church and I’m supposed to sit still, or I’m here waiting at the clinic, or even just sitting around at home, I start feeling trapped in my own skin. I’ll try to tell myself, “Just sit here, just be still,” but then I feel like I have to get up, move around, do something with my hands, walk somewhere—something. It’s not always attached to a specific worry. It’s just this pressure to move.
Has this need to move and feeling of restlessness been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this a new change that started fairly recently?

No, it’s not really new. I mean, the way I feel it now as an adult is maybe different because I’m supposed to act grown and sit through things, but if I’m being honest, I was like this even when I was a boy in school.

Teachers were always moving my seat around because I couldn’t stay put. Like they’d put me closer to the front, then away from somebody I was talking to, then somewhere else, and it never really fixed it. I’d be talking out of turn, blurting stuff before I was supposed to, and I remember getting in trouble for jumping up before class was even done, like I just couldn’t wait or hold myself still until they said we could go.

So yeah… this goes way back. It’s not like it just suddenly started recently.
